The 4OMe deceleration — every progress curve

4OMe-BnOH · catalysed · phosphate

All 92 live cuvettes of the 4OMe catalysed, phosphate block — the one the discrimination needs, because a single progress curve cannot tell time from product and the separation exists only across curves. The rust line is whichever form the curve earned; nothing is excluded and every fit uses every point except the instrument's discarded first reading. The driver regression the analysis quotes runs on 84 of them — the ones whose fall is measurable at all — so the 8 that are here and not there are visible rather than dropped silently.

The shaded band is the tail slowdown.sink_fit actually read, and rate max (rolling rate) is where it begins — the rolling rate's maximum, which the data chooses rather than the analyst, and which is a different estimator from the progress fit drawn over it. Its width is SINK_WINDOW = 0.15 of the run, and section 4's window sweep is the reason that number is quoted with a systematic rather than an error: a wider window smooths the slow cold curves more than the fast warm ones. 41 of 92 curves decline far enough, over a long enough tail, to be read this way; the rest say so in their footer.

The dashed verticals are the progress fit's own clocks and the dotted line its asymptote c − ΣB + v_ss·t, drawn the same way in every folder (figure_kit.progress_panel). v_peak is marked on the derivative strip, which is where the deceleration this folder is about is directly visible: the strip falls away to the right on every catalysed 4OMe curve.
